paper.title_en: Electro-Penrose Process in Charged BTZ Black Holes: From Probe Limit to Thermodynamic Backreaction
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the electro-Penrose process (EPP) in $(2+1)$-dimensional charged Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) spacetime, from probe-limit particle dynamics to quasistatic thermodynamic backreaction. In the probe background, neutral particles have no exterior circular orbits, and charged circular motion requires a minimum repulsive coupling. We derive the maximum single-event energy at fixed decay data, including fragment masses and charge allocation, and check capture and collection at a finite receiver in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. Repetitive radial extraction on successive exact stationary backgrounds uses an adaptive incident specific charge. The continuum mass-charge path identifies the switch between incident turning-point and negative-energy stopping, supported by numerical checks. The prescribed sequences terminate at nonzero residual charge before exhausting the energy reservoir, providing a protocol-dependent third-law analogy. The consumed reservoir is divided between extracted energy and irreversible growth of irreducible mass, with proportions depending on the protocol.
